questions.q: What does a debug log's CUMULATIVE_LIMIT_USAGE section report?
options: A prediction of how the code will perform on a different org
The total number of users currently logged into the org
The real, measured governor limit usage (SOQL queries, DML statements, CPU time, heap, etc.) for that specific transaction's execution
A list of every validation rule that exists on the object, regardless of whether it fired
questions.explain: CUMULATIVE_LIMIT_USAGE is the platform's own measured account of exactly how much of each governor limit that specific transaction consumed — not an estimate.

questions.q: What is the maximum size of an individual Salesforce debug log, and what happens if a transaction would exceed it?
options: 5 MB; the transaction itself fails to complete
There is no size cap on debug logs
100 MB; the excess is automatically emailed to the org administrator
20 MB; the log is truncated by removing older lines, which can happen anywhere in the log, not only at the start
questions.explain: Salesforce's documentation sets a 20 MB per-log cap. A log exceeding that is truncated by removing older lines from anywhere in the log, which can leave gaps in the middle rather than just cutting off the end.

questions.q: What is the retention period for system-generated debug logs versus logs captured for monitoring?
options: 24 hours for system-generated logs, 7 days for monitoring logs
7 days for system-generated logs, 24 hours for monitoring logs
30 days for both types of logs
Debug logs are retained permanently unless manually deleted
questions.explain: Salesforce's documentation specifies 24-hour retention for system debug logs and 7-day retention for logs captured specifically for monitoring purposes.

questions.q: Why can setting every trace flag log category to its most verbose level (FINEST) actually hurt a debugging effort?
options: FINEST level logging is not a real option in Salesforce and would cause an error
It makes the log more likely to hit the 20 MB truncation cap exactly when the detail is needed, and buries the specific relevant lines under a much larger volume of unrelated output
Verbose logging automatically disables the CUMULATIVE_LIMIT_USAGE section
It has no real downside; more detail is always strictly better for debugging
questions.explain: Maximum verbosity across every category increases the risk of hitting the 20 MB truncation cap and makes the specific lines you need (like CUMULATIVE_LIMIT_USAGE) harder to find amid unrelated detail — targeting only the relevant categories is more effective.

questions.q: What org-wide safeguard exists if debug log generation gets too high across an org?
options: The org is automatically suspended until an administrator manually intervenes
All Apex execution across the org is halted until logs are cleared
If log generation exceeds 1,000 MB within a 15-minute window, trace flags are automatically disabled, and the affected users are emailed that they can re-enable logging after 15 minutes
There is no org-wide safeguard; individual logs can grow without limit
questions.explain: Salesforce throttles excessive org-wide log generation: crossing the 1,000 MB-per-15-minutes threshold auto-disables trace flags and notifies the users who set them, rather than letting log volume grow unchecked.
